title: Add pre-commit hook for vendor file protection
body:
Add a pre-commit hook that enforces the same vendor file protection as the check-vendor GHA workflow, vendored to consumer repos via install.sh.

## Design

- Add `--staged` flag to `vendored/check` — checks `git diff --cached --name-only` (staged files) instead of branch diff
- Create `vendored/hooks/pre-commit` — thin shell script calling `python3 .vendored/check --staged`
- Add `--install-hook` flag to `vendored/check` — symlinks `.vendored/hooks/pre-commit` into `.git/hooks/pre-commit`, force-overwriting any existing hook (including pearls)
- Update `install.sh` to download the hook to `.vendored/hooks/pre-commit`

## Acceptance criteria

### `--staged` mode
- [ ] `vendored/check --staged` checks staged files via `git diff --cached --name-only`
- [ ] Reuses all existing protection logic (patterns, allowed lists, install-branch skip)
- [ ] Exits 0 if no staged violations, 1 if violations found
- [ ] Works both in CI and locally (no dependency on GitHub env vars)

### `vendored/hooks/pre-commit`
- [ ] Shell script at `vendored/hooks/pre-commit` that runs `python3 .vendored/check --staged`
- [ ] Exits with the check script exit code
- [ ] Executable permissions set

### `--install-hook` mode
- [ ] `vendored/check --install-hook` symlinks `.git/hooks/pre-commit` to `.vendored/hooks/pre-commit` (relative: `../../.vendored/hooks/pre-commit`)
- [ ] Force-overwrites any existing pre-commit hook (file or symlink) — squashes pearls etc.
- [ ] Verifies `.vendored/hooks/pre-commit` exists before symlinking, errors if missing
- [ ] Prints confirmation message on success

### install.sh
- [ ] Downloads `vendored/hooks/pre-commit` to `.vendored/hooks/pre-commit`
- [ ] Sets executable permissions (`chmod +x`)
- [ ] Creates `.vendored/hooks/` directory

### Tests
- [ ] Unit tests for `--staged` mode in `tests/test_check.py` (staged files checked, protection logic applied, violations reported)
- [ ] Unit test for `--install-hook` (symlink created, overwrites existing, errors on missing hook file)

### Docs
- [ ] Update `install.sh` header comment to document the new hook file
- [ ] Add `--staged` and `--install-hook` to the check script docstring

title: Vendor dependency management
body:
Extend the vendor contract to support vendor-to-vendor dependencies. Vendors declare which other vendors they require via an optional deps.json at repo root, and the framework checks (and optionally installs) those dependencies during the install flow.

## Motivation

Today, if vendor A requires vendor B to function, there's no way to express or enforce this. The failure mode is silent: vendor A installs fine, then breaks at runtime because vendor B isn't present. Consumers have to debug missing deps themselves; vendor authors resort to README notes.

## Key Design Decisions

- **deps.json at repo root** (not emitted by install.sh) — deps must be checked before running install.sh
- **Match deps by repo field**, not vendor name — handles consumers who install with custom --name
- **Dependency modes**: error (default, safe), warn, install (auto-install), skip
- **Version constraints deferred** — v1 is presence-only
- **Topological sort for install all** — prevents ordering failures
- **Cache resolved deps** in .vendored/manifests/<vendor>.deps for reverse-dep lookups

## Planning Doc

docs/planning/dependency-management.md

title: Multi-vendor PR commit fails: pre-commit hook blocks chore/install-vendors branch
body:
## Problem

When multiple vendors update simultaneously (e.g., git-semver + git-vendored), `create_pull_request()` in `.vendored/install` fails with `CalledProcessError` on `git commit`.

**Root cause:** The multi-vendor branch name `chore/install-vendors` (line 636) does not match any individual vendor's `install_branch` prefix (e.g., `chore/install-git-vendored`, `chore/install-git-semver`). The pre-commit hook runs `.vendored/check --staged`, which checks branch matching at `check_vendor()` line 181 — since no prefix matches, it treats all staged vendor files as protection violations and exits 1.

Single-vendor updates work because their branch name (e.g., `chore/install-git-vendored-v0.0.11`) starts with the vendor's `install_branch`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `create_pull_request()` succeeds when multiple vendors update simultaneously
- [ ] The fix uses `git commit --no-verify` in `create_pull_request()` since the install script IS the authorized mechanism for modifying vendor files (the pre-commit hook guards against manual edits, not automated installs)
- [ ] Add a code comment explaining why `--no-verify` is used
- [ ] Add a test that verifies `create_pull_request` passes `--no-verify` to git commit
- [ ] Existing single-vendor PR creation still works

## Reproduction

Run `python3 .vendored/install all --pr` when 2+ vendors have updates available, with the pre-commit hook installed. The `git commit` step in `create_pull_request()` will fail with exit code 1.

## Files to Change

- `.vendored/install` line 681: add `--no-verify` flag to git commit
- `tests/` — add test coverage for multi-vendor commit with pre-commit hook

title: Use git push --force-with-lease for ephemeral install branches
body:
## Problem
`create_pull_request()` does a plain `git push -u origin <branch>`, which
fails as a non-fast-forward when the ephemeral install branch (e.g.
`chore/install-vendors`) already exists on the remote from a prior run.

## Fix
Change to `git push --force-with-lease -u origin <branch>`.

This is safe because these branches are ephemeral automation branches, not
shared work. `--force-with-lease` still guards against the edge case where
someone else pushed to the branch concurrently.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `templates/install` push command uses `--force-with-lease`
- [ ] `.vendored/install` push command uses `--force-with-lease`
- [ ] Brief inline comment explaining why force-with-lease is appropriate
- [ ] Test asserts `--force-with-lease` is present in the push command

title: Exclude workflow files from automated install PR commits
body:
## Problem
`create_pull_request()` runs `git add -A` which stages `.github/workflows/`
files written by install.sh. The `GITHUB_TOKEN` used in CI lacks `workflows`
permission, so `git push` is rejected with:

> refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow without
> `workflows` permission

## Root cause
install.sh always installs workflow templates (lines 112-113) and includes
them in the manifest. `git add -A` blindly stages everything. These workflow
files should only be installed during initial bootstrap, not re-committed in
automated update PRs.

## Fix
After `git add -A`, run `git reset HEAD -- .github/workflows/` to unstage
workflow files before committing. This keeps install.sh's behavior unchanged
(it still writes them to disk for initial installs) but excludes them from
the automated PR commit.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `create_pull_request()` unstages `.github/workflows/` after `git add -A`
- [ ] Both `templates/install` and `.vendored/install` are updated
- [ ] Test verifies `git reset HEAD -- .github/workflows/` is called
- [ ] Existing tests still pass

title: Self-bootstrap coordinator on git-vendored install
body:
## Problem
When any consumer repo updates git-vendored, the OLD `.vendored/install`
coordinator runs in memory while the NEW `install.sh` writes the fixed
coordinator to disk. Post-install steps (PR creation, output) execute
using the OLD in-memory code. If the OLD coordinator has a bug in those
post-install paths, the install fails, the fix never gets committed, and
the repo is stuck indefinitely.

Example: the force-push fix in `create_pull_request()` — install.sh wrote
the fixed coordinator to disk, but the old `create_pull_request()` was
still executing in memory.

## Root cause
`download_and_run_install()` runs the vendor's install.sh, which overwrites
`.vendored/install` on disk. But the Python process continues executing the
old version from memory. There is no mechanism to hand off to the new
coordinator for post-install steps.

## Solution
After `download_and_run_install()` returns, detect that the on-disk
`.vendored/install` has changed (hash comparison against `__file__`).
If changed, re-exec the process:

```
python3 .vendored/install git-vendored --pr --post-install-only
```

The `--post-install-only` flag tells the NEW coordinator to skip
`download_and_run_install()` and only run post-install steps (build
result from on-disk manifest/version state, create PR, write output).

### Flow
1. `python3 .vendored/install git-vendored --pr` (OLD coordinator)
2. OLD coordinator calls `download_and_run_install()` → new install.sh
   writes new coordinator to disk
3. OLD coordinator detects `.vendored/install` on disk differs from
   running script (hash comparison)
4. OLD coordinator re-execs:
   `python3 .vendored/install git-vendored --pr --post-install-only`
5. NEW coordinator sees `--post-install-only`, reads version/manifest
   from disk, creates PR

### Scope
This is specifically for git-vendored updating its own coordinator.
No other vendor's install.sh writes to `.vendored/install`, so no
generalization is needed. Detection should key off whether the on-disk
coordinator actually changed, not vendor name or dogfood flag.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Add `--post-install-only` flag to CLI argument parser
- [ ] After `download_and_run_install()`, hash-compare `__file__` against
      on-disk `.vendored/install`; if changed, re-exec with `--post-install-only`
      and forward all relevant flags (--pr, --version, --force)
- [ ] `--post-install-only` code path reads installed version and manifest
      from disk, builds result dict, runs PR creation and output
- [ ] Guard against infinite re-exec (e.g. if `--post-install-only` is set,
      never re-exec again)
- [ ] Add tests for the bootstrap detection and re-exec path
- [ ] Update docs if install CLI reference exists

Create `.vendored/lib/vendor-helpers.sh` — a shell library that vendor `install.sh` scripts can source to avoid duplicating download/auth/manifest logic.

title: Implement --setup-hooks for multi-agent hook orchestration
body:
## Summary

New command `python3 .vendored/install --setup-hooks [agent]` that generates agent-specific config files pointing to a framework-owned orchestrator. Supports Claude Code and Codex. Moves hook orchestration ownership from madreperla to git-vendored.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `--setup-hooks [agent]` on `.vendored/install`:
  - `agent` = `claude`, `codex`, or omitted (auto-detect based on which dotdir exists; no-op if neither)
  - For Claude: generates/updates `.claude/settings.json` with SessionStart/resume hooks pointing to `.vendored/hooks/vendored-session.sh`
  - For Codex: generates/updates `.codex/config.toml` with SessionStart hook (format per Codex v0.114.0+ experimental hooks)
  - Idempotent — safe to re-run after vendor install/remove
- [ ] Move orchestrator from `.claude/hooks/vendored-session.sh` to `.vendored/hooks/vendored-session.sh`
  - Replace `PROJECT_DIR` derivation: use `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` instead of directory traversal
  - Keep backward compat: if old path exists, remove it during migration
- [ ] Orchestrator is in git-vendored's own manifest (framework-owned file)
- [ ] Agent config files (`.claude/settings.json`, `.codex/config.toml`) are NOT in any manifest — they're project-owned, framework-generated
- [ ] Bootstrap `install.sh` runs `--setup-hooks` after initial install
- [ ] Tests covering: Claude setup, Codex setup, auto-detect, no-op when no agent dirs, idempotency, orchestrator path migration

## Vendor Repo Prereqs

### mangimangi/pearls (non-blocking, needed for Codex end-to-end)

Replace `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` fallback with `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` in 4 hook files:

**Files to change:**
- `.vendored/pkg/pearls/hooks/session-start.sh` (or source equivalent)
- `.vendored/pkg/pearls/hooks/session-resume.sh`
- `.vendored/pkg/pearls/hooks/post-install.sh`
- `.vendored/pkg/pearls/hooks/pre-push`

```bash

# After:
PROJECT_DIR="${PROJECT_DIR:-$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)}"
```

One-line change per file. No functional change in practice — `$PROJECT_DIR` is already set by the orchestrator. But without this, hooks fail when invoked by Codex (which doesn't set `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`).

body:
## Problem

The --pr codepath in .vendored/install creates PRs that are missing .vendored/pkg/<vendor>/ files. Manifests, configs, and hooks are committed, but the actual vendor code (prl.py, AGENTS.md, hook scripts, etc.) is not.

Discovered in medici PR #5 — GHA install of madreperla (with pearls as a dependency) produced a PR with 12 files, none from .vendored/pkg/.

## Root cause

When self-bootstrap triggers a re-exec with --post-install-only (line 1496-1517), the new process only builds a result for args.target (the main vendor). Dependency files are on disk (written by the initial install), and git add -A (line 980) stages them, but the --post-install-only path was designed for single-vendor re-execs, not dependency multi-vendor installs. The result metadata only reflects the main vendor.

Worth investigating:
1. Does git add -A actually stage pkg/ files, or is there a working directory issue?
2. Does the dependency install (pearls) complete before or after _maybe_reexec triggers?
3. The --post-install-only path should detect ALL changed vendors by scanning manifests, not just args.target.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When --pr is used with --deps=install, the PR includes all .vendored/pkg/ files for both the main vendor and its dependencies
- [ ] The --post-install-only path aggregates results for all vendors that were installed (main + deps)
- [ ] Test: mock a vendor with a dependency, run install with --pr --deps=install, verify PR diff includes pkg/ files for both

title: --private flag doesn't propagate through dependency auto-install
body:
## Problem

When installing a private vendor with --deps=install, the coordinator auto-installs dependencies via resolve_deps → install_new_vendor. But the dependency's private status is unknown:

1. The dep has no per-vendor config yet (first-time install in the consumer repo)
2. The dep's entry in deps.json has no private field — it only contains repo and optionally version
3. install_new_vendor doesn't receive a private flag, so get_auth_token falls back to GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN instead of VENDOR_PAT

Even though the parent's token is passed through (which may be VENDOR_PAT), get_auth_token inside install_existing_vendor checks vendor_config.get("private") to decide whether VENDOR_PAT is required. For a new dep with no config, this check fails.

## Example

madreperla depends on pearls (private repo). In the consumer repo:

  VENDOR_PAT=<token> python3 .vendored/install mangimangi/madreperla --private --deps=install

The coordinator has auth for madreperla, but when it auto-installs pearls, there's no pearls.json config yet, so the coordinator doesn't know pearls needs VENDOR_PAT.

## Fix options

1. **Per-dep private declaration in deps.json**: Allow deps.json to include a private field per dependency:
   ```json
   {"pearls": {"repo": "mangimangi/pearls", "private": true}}
   ```
   resolve_deps passes this to install_new_vendor which uses it for get_auth_token.

2. **Inherit parent's --private flag**: If the parent is private, assume deps are too. Simple but incorrect when a private vendor depends on a public one (over-requires VENDOR_PAT).

3. **Both**: Per-dep declaration with parent flag as fallback.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] deps.json supports an optional private field per dependency
- [ ] resolve_deps passes the private flag to install_new_vendor when auto-installing
- [ ] install_new_vendor uses the private flag for get_auth_token on first-time dep installs
- [ ] Test: mock a private vendor with a private dependency, verify --deps=install works with only VENDOR_PAT set
- [ ] Docs: update vendor contract section to document the private field in deps.json

title: Migrate docs to .pearls/docs/ and simplify providers config
body:
Atomic migration: move planning docs to `.pearls/docs/`, simplify `madreperla.yaml` providers, and regenerate commands. Per the planning doc, this is one issue because partial states (e.g. moved docs but old providers config) would break command generation.

## Scope

### 1. Update pearls.yaml

Add top-level `docs:` section mapping each doc category to its `.pearls/docs/` path:

```yaml
docs:
  planning: .pearls/docs
  epics: .pearls/docs/epics
  ideas: .pearls/docs/ideas
  headaches: .pearls/docs/headaches
  retros: .pearls/docs/retros
```

### 2. Move doc directories

- `mkdir -p .pearls/docs/retros`
- `git mv docs/planning/epics .pearls/docs/epics` (skip if absent)
- `git mv docs/planning/ideas .pearls/docs/ideas` (skip if absent)
- `git mv docs/planning/headaches .pearls/docs/headaches` (skip if absent)
- Move any standalone `docs/planning/*.md` files to `.pearls/docs/` root (e.g. `gh-extension.md`)
- `touch .pearls/docs/retros/.gitkeep`
- `rmdir docs/planning` if empty

Use `2>/dev/null || true` on `git mv` / `rmdir` so missing dirs don't abort the migration.

### 3. Simplify madreperla.yaml

Replace the existing `providers:` block with:

```yaml
providers:
  issues: pearls
  docs: pearls
```

Leave `docs: [AGENTS.md, README.md, docs/]` (the repo context list) unchanged.

### 4. Regenerate

- `prl configure`
- `madp configure --provider claude`

### 5. Verify

- `grep -r '{docs\.' commands/` must find nothing (no unresolved `{docs.*}` literals in generated commands).

## Acceptance criteria

- `.pearls/docs/` contains `epics/`, `ideas/`, `headaches/`, `retros/` subdirs (retros has `.gitkeep`).
- No `docs/planning/epics/`, `docs/planning/ideas/`, `docs/planning/headaches/` directories remain.
- `docs/planning/` is empty or removed; any standalone `.md` files have moved to `.pearls/docs/`.
- `madreperla.yaml` `providers:` block is simplified to `{issues: pearls, docs: pearls}`.
- `pearls.yaml` has a `docs:` section pointing at `.pearls/docs/` paths.
- Generated commands under `commands/` have fully resolved paths (no `{docs.*}` literals).
- All changes committed and pushed in a single commit.

title: Git-semver files audit
body:
# Git-semver files audit

> Epic: `mdci-dev-2153` (orchestrator), per-repo plan for `git-vendored`

## Problem

The `.vendored/configs/git-semver.json` configuration may be missing entries for user-facing shipped files — command MDs, mode files, doc files, and other artifacts that should trigger a version bump when changed. Missing entries mean changes to these files don't bump the version, leading to stale version numbers that don't reflect actual changes.

## In scope for this repo

Audit `.vendored/configs/git-semver.json` in this repo:

1. Identify all user-facing shipped files: command MDs, mode files, doc files, and any other files that end users or downstream consumers interact with
2. Compare against the current `files` entries in git-semver.json
3. Add any missing file patterns that should trigger version bumps
4. Remove any stale patterns that reference files no longer present

## Reference context (handled elsewhere)

- The same audit is being performed independently in all 6 repos (pearls, madreperla, medici, git-vendored, git-semver, git-dogfood) under this epic. Each repo's audit is self-contained.

## Acceptance criteria

1. All user-facing shipped files are covered by git-semver.json file patterns
2. No stale patterns referencing non-existent files
3. `git-semver check` passes with the updated config

## Out of scope

- Changing git-semver's behavior or configuration schema
- Adding new file types not currently shipped

## Risk notes

- Overly broad glob patterns could trigger unnecessary version bumps on non-user-facing changes. Prefer specific patterns over wildcards where practical.

title: git-vendored's own pull request checks run through git-cicd
body:
Unit 3 of plan `git-dev-883c` (record: `mangimangi/git-dev`, `.pearls/docs/epics/git-dev-883c.md`), agreed with the owner on 2026-11-28. Delivers into `plan/git-dev-883c`.

## What happens today

git-vendored's pull request checks are two hand-written GitHub Actions workflows:

- `.github/workflows/test.yml` ("Tests"): on pull requests, sets up Python `3.x`, `pip install pytest pyyaml`, runs `python3 -m pytest tests/ -v`. No Python version was ever chosen: `3.x` is whatever is newest, and the repository declares no Python floor anywhere (it has no `pyproject.toml`).
- `.github/workflows/check-vendor.yml` ("Check Vendor Files"): on every pull request, `python3 .vendored/check` with full history. It is installed and protected by git-vendored.

git-cicd v0.0.3 is installed (`.vendored/pkg/git-cicd/`, `.vendored/configs/git-cicd.json` with no jobs; pull request #120), but the install delivered no `.github/workflows/git-cicd-open.yml`: an install pull request never carries workflow files. So nothing runs through git-cicd yet.

## Required behaviour

git-vendored's own pull request checks are declared as git-cicd jobs and run through it, the way git-cicd's own repository does (`mangimangi/git-cicd`: `.vendored/configs/git-cicd.json`, `ci/setup.sh`, `ci/test.sh`, README "The config" and "Installing").

- `.vendored/configs/git-cicd.json` declares an `open` job for the tests, with a setup script that installs what the suite needs on the Python floor the repository declares and a step that runs it, and an `open` job whose step is `.vendored/check`. `paths` and `needs_nothing` are chosen so documents and tracker records need no job.
- The generated workflow exists: `.vendored/pkg/git-cicd/git-cicd generate` is run and `.github/workflows/git-cicd-open.yml` committed (it is listed as editable for the vendor check).
- No Python version is written in any workflow; the repository declares its Python floor in one place (a `pyproject.toml` with `requires-python`, as the other tools do), and it is the floor the tests actually pass on, found by running them on it.
- `.github/workflows/test.yml` is removed. `validate-vendor.yml` is left as it is (a later unit moves it).
- `AGENTS.md` and `README.md` say how the checks run here (`.vendored/pkg/git-cicd/git-cicd check --setup`, then `check`).

Do not add, change or delete a vendor-protected file: `check-vendor.yml`, `version-bump.yml`, `install-vendored.yml`, `dogfood.yml` and everything a manifest under `.vendored/manifests/` lists stay as they are. The vendor check runs twice for now (the old workflow and the new job); the planning session removes the old one later. Run `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-883c` before finishing and undo anything it reports.

## Acceptance criteria

- The pull request into `plan/git-dev-883c` shows `Open / <name> / git-vendored:<job>` rows for the test job and the vendor check job, `Open / Decide / git-cicd:decide`, `Open / Report / git-cicd:report`, and the commit status `Verdict / git-cicd:verdict` is success. The status is a commit status, not a check run: read it from the commit's statuses.
- `.vendored/pkg/git-cicd/git-cicd validate` prints `config ok: 2 jobs` (or more), and `verify` passes.
- `.vendored/pkg/git-cicd/git-cicd check --setup` passes in a clean checkout.
- The tests pass on the Python version `requires-python` names as the floor, shown by the job's setup installing that version.
- `.github/workflows/test.yml` no longer exists; no other file under `.github/workflows/` except `git-cicd-open.yml` is changed.
- `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-883c` reports nothing.

title: git-vendored bumps its version in the pull request and tags on merge; an upgrade does not put removed workflows back
body:
Unit 13 of plan `git-dev-883c` (record: `mangimangi/git-dev`, `.pearls/docs/epics/git-dev-883c.md`; the design is in `mangimangi/git-dev`, `.pearls/docs/what-reaches-main-policy.md`). Added by the owner on 2026-11-28. Delivers into `plan/git-dev-883c`.

## What happens today

git-vendored releases after a merge by pushing to the branch that was just merged into. Its `release` job (`merge` on `main`, in `.vendored/configs/git-cicd.json`) runs `.vendored/pkg/git-semver/release` with no subcommand, in its default bump-on-merge mode: a merge that touched the configured `files` is bumped, committed as `chore: bump version vX.Y.Z` and pushed to `main`. With `main` protected the push is refused and a bump pull request is opened with the workflow's own token; GitHub starts no workflows for it, so it has no checks and has to be merged by hand before anything is tagged. The commit that is finally tagged is the bump commit, which ran no checks.

git-semver v0.1.0 or later, installed here, offers the other way (`mangimangi/git-semver` README, "bump in the pull request"): `git-semver check-bump` fails a pull request that changes a configured file without raising the version, and with `"bump_on": "pull_request"` in the git-semver config `release` tags the landed commit with the version it carries and creates the GitHub release, pushing nothing to the branch and moving no `latest` tag. git-semver's own repository released v0.1.0 this way on 2026-11-28.

## Required behaviour

git-vendored releases the way git-semver's own repository does (`mangimangi/git-semver`: `.vendored/configs/git-semver.json`, `.vendored/configs/git-cicd.json`):

- `.vendored/configs/git-semver.json` sets `"bump_on": "pull_request"`.
- `.vendored/configs/git-cicd.json` gains an `open` job for pull requests into `main` whose step is `.vendored/pkg/git-semver/git-semver check-bump`, and the `release` job's step is `.vendored/pkg/git-semver/release` with no subcommand. A script under `ci/` that only existed to choose between bump and publish is removed with its tests; the manual run of `release` keeps working as git-semver defines it for this mode, and inputs that no longer apply are removed from the job's declaration.
- The version file is raised in this change, with the changelog entry if the repository keeps one, so that the integration branch carries a version higher than `main`'s: the pull request into `main` is then this repository's first release made this way. Use `.vendored/pkg/git-semver/git-semver bump` for it; a patch bump unless the changes since the last release include one that breaks an adopter, in which case say so in the pull request and bump accordingly.
- `.vendored/pkg/git-cicd/git-cicd generate` is run if the config change alters a generated workflow, and what it writes is committed; `verify` passes.
- `README.md` and `AGENTS.md` say how a release happens here now: a change to a configured file raises the version in the same pull request, with which command; merging into `main` tags and publishes it; nothing is pushed to `main`.

Do not add, change or delete a vendor-protected file. Run `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-883c` before finishing.

## Acceptance criteria

- `.vendored/pkg/git-cicd/git-cicd validate` reports the version check job; `verify` passes; `.vendored/pkg/git-cicd/git-cicd check` passes with coverage at 99% or more and the bats tests green.
- `.vendored/pkg/git-semver/git-semver check-bump` passes for this change against `origin/main`, and fails when the version file is reset to `main`'s (shown once in the pull request description).
- The version file on the unit's branch is higher than on `main`.
- No script, test or doc still describes the bump commit, the bump pull request or the `chore: bump version` rule as how this repository releases.
- The pull request into `plan/git-dev-883c` has a passing `Verdict / git-cicd:verdict`.
- `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-883c` reports nothing.

## Also in this unit: an upgrade must not put removed workflows back

`install.sh` installs `check-vendor.yml` and `install-vendored.yml` whenever they are absent (`install_workflow`, around lines 95-105: "skip if already present"), taking "absent" to mean "first install". A repository that runs the vendor check and the update as git-cicd jobs has removed them on purpose, and every upgrade of git-vendored writes them back to disk; with an install pull request that now carries workflow files when its token may write them, they would return to the repository as protected files. (The same defect was seen in git-semver's installer on 2026-11-28 and is fixed there separately.)

Required: an upgrade never adds either workflow; they are installed only on the bootstrap install into a repository with no earlier git-vendored install, and not when the repository's git-cicd config already declares jobs whose steps run `.vendored/check` and `.vendored/install` (the installer says why in one line). The manifest never lists a file that is not there. Tests (bats, no network) show a bootstrap, an upgrade without the workflows, and a repository on git-cicd; the README states the rule.

title: An install pull request is opened with VENDOR_PAT when it is set; no test reads a real token
body:
Unit 17 of plan `git-dev-883c` (record: `mangimangi/git-dev`, `.pearls/docs/epics/git-dev-883c.md`; the policy is in `mangimangi/git-dev`, `.pearls/docs/what-reaches-main-policy.md`). Found on 2026-11-28 when the owner ran git-cicd's `update-vendored` job with a `VENDOR_PAT` in place. Delivers into `plan/git-dev-883c`.

## What happens today

In `--pr` mode the installer opens its pull request with the workflow's own token even when a `VENDOR_PAT` is set. `templates/install` builds the environment for `gh` from `GITHUB_TOKEN` (around lines 1316-1318: `github_token = os.environ.get("GITHUB_TOKEN", "")`, then `gh_env["GH_TOKEN"] = github_token`), overriding a `GH_TOKEN` the caller set, and uses it for `gh pr create` and for `gh pr merge --auto`. Since v0.0.30 the *push* is made with `VENDOR_PAT` when it is set (so workflow files can be carried), but the pull request is still opened as GitHub Actions.

Two consequences, both seen:

- GitHub starts no workflows for a pull request opened with a workflow's own token. An install pull request therefore has no checks, and where the default branch requires the `Verdict / git-cicd:verdict` status it can never be merged (git-vendored #131 was opened by `github-actions[bot]` with zero check runs).
- Where a repository does not let Actions open pull requests, the install fails after pushing its branch: `Failed to create PR: pull request create failed: GraphQL: GitHub Actions is not permitted to create or approve pull requests (createPullRequest)` (git-cicd, run on 2026-11-28 05:23 UTC, with `VENDOR_PAT: ***` in the job's environment). The branch `chore/install-git-semver-v0.1.1` was left pushed with no pull request.

The agreed policy is that a pull request a machine opens is opened with a token that starts workflows.

## Required behaviour

- In `--pr` mode, when `VENDOR_PAT` is set, the pull request is opened with it, and auto-merge (when the vendor asks for it) is requested with it. Without `VENDOR_PAT` the behaviour is as today.
- When the pull request cannot be opened after the branch was pushed, the installer says so with the branch name and how to open it by hand, and exits non-zero; when a pull request for that branch already exists it is reused, as today.
- When the pull request was opened with the workflow's own token, its description says in one line that no checks will run on it and that a `VENDOR_PAT` secret changes that.
- No token value is printed.
- `README.md` ("How Updates Work", the authentication table) says which token does what: reading a private vendor, pushing the install branch with workflow files, opening the pull request so that checks run.
- `VERSION` is raised in this change (a patch), as the `version-check` job requires.

Do not add, change or delete a vendor-protected file (this repository's own `.vendored/install` is an installed copy; change `templates/install`). Run `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-883c` before finishing.

## Acceptance criteria

- Tests (no network; `git push` and `gh` replaced at the boundary the existing tests use) show `gh pr create` and `gh pr merge --auto` run with `VENDOR_PAT` as `GH_TOKEN` when it is set, and with the workflow's token when it is not; the description line appears only in the second case; a failed `gh pr create` after a push names the branch and exits non-zero.
- `.vendored/pkg/git-cicd/git-cicd check --setup` passes with coverage at 99% or more for every shipped Python script, and the bats tests green; `verify` passes.
- `.vendored/pkg/git-semver/git-semver check-bump` passes against `origin/main`.
- The pull request into `plan/git-dev-883c` has a passing `Verdict / git-cicd:verdict`.
- `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-883c` reports nothing.

## A first attempt failed in CI, and what it showed (read before starting)

An earlier attempt at this unit (`gv-0232`, pull request #135, closed unmerged) passed in the session's container and failed in CI on one test, `tests/test_install.py::TestCreatePullRequest::test_uses_github_token_for_gh`. The test set `GITHUB_TOKEN` and `GH_TOKEN` and expected `gh` to be given `GITHUB_TOKEN`, but did not remove `VENDOR_PAT` from its environment. In CI the job's environment holds the repository's real `VENDOR_PAT`, so the new code (correctly) chose it and the assertion failed.

Worse, the failed assertion printed the value: pytest's shortened comparison showed the first and last characters of the real token in a public Actions log (`assert 'github_pat_1...<13 characters>' == 'repo-token'`). GitHub masks a secret only where the whole value appears; a shortened value is not masked.

So, in addition to the behaviour above:

- No test may read a token from the ambient environment. Every test that exercises token selection runs with `VENDOR_PAT`, `GH_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` removed first and then sets the fake values it needs; do this once for the whole suite (an autouse fixture in `tests/conftest.py`, and the equivalent in the bats helpers) rather than per test, so a new test cannot forget it.
- Add a test that fails if that guard is removed: with a `VENDOR_PAT` in the outer environment, a test body sees none.
- Tests assert on fake token values only, and the suite passes when run with real-looking values exported in the outer environment for all three variables (run it that way once and say so in the pull request).
- Update or replace `test_uses_github_token_for_gh` to state the new rule in both directions (with and without `VENDOR_PAT`).

title: The installer reads CICD_WRITE_TOKEN and CICD_READ_TOKEN; a missing write token is a loud failure
body:
Unit 3 of plan `git-dev-aef7` (record: `mangimangi/git-dev`, `.pearls/docs/epics/git-dev-aef7.md`), agreed with the owner on 2026-11-28. Delivers into `plan/git-dev-aef7`.

## What happens today

The installer knows one personal token, `VENDOR_PAT`, and uses it for two different things: to read a private vendor repository (`templates/install` lines 210-212, `templates/lib/vendor-helpers.sh`), and, in `--pr` mode, to push the install branch with workflow files, open the pull request and request auto-merge (lines 1301-1325, 1350-1387, 1435). `templates/install` names it 14 times, the README 11, `ci/update-vendored.sh` 3.

The owner has decided to rename it and split it by what a token can do: `CICD_WRITE_TOKEN` (proposes changes: pushes branches, opens pull requests, writes workflow files) and `CICD_READ_TOKEN` (reads private repositories; cannot write). git-cicd will give a job a secret only if the job declares it (unit 1 of the plan), with the old name accepted for a time.

And when no write token is there, the installer in CI still opens the pull request with the workflow's own token. GitHub starts no workflows for such a pull request, so it has no checks and, where the default branch requires a verdict, can never be merged; where Actions may not open pull requests, the run fails after pushing its branch. This has caught the owner three times in one day.

## Required behaviour

- To push the install branch, carry workflow files, open the pull request and request auto-merge, the installer uses `CICD_WRITE_TOKEN`, and `VENDOR_PAT` when the new name is unset.
- To read a private vendor it uses `CICD_READ_TOKEN`, then `CICD_WRITE_TOKEN`, then `VENDOR_PAT`.
- In `--pr` mode under CI (`GITHUB_ACTIONS` set), with no write token available, the installer does not quietly open a pull request that will get no checks: it fails before changing anything, with a message that names the secret, says that a git-cicd job must declare it, and names the documented flag that asks for the old behaviour on purpose. With that flag, and outside CI, behaviour is as today.
- Every message, the pull request description and the README name the new secrets; the README has one table of which token does what and which permissions a fine-grained token needs for it, and says `VENDOR_PAT` is still read, as deprecated.
- This repository's `ci/update-vendored.sh` uses `CICD_WRITE_TOKEN`, then `VENDOR_PAT`.
- No token value is printed. The suite's token guard (`tests/conftest.py`, the bats helpers) removes the two new names as well as `VENDOR_PAT`, `GH_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
- `VERSION` is raised in this change (a patch) with its changelog entry if the repository keeps one, as the `version-check` job requires.

Do not add, change or delete a vendor-protected file (this repository's own `.vendored/install` is an installed copy; change `templates/install`). Run `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-aef7` before finishing.

## Acceptance criteria

- Tests (no network; `git push` and `gh` replaced at the boundary the existing tests use) show, for the push, the pull request and auto-merge: `CICD_WRITE_TOKEN` is used when set; `VENDOR_PAT` when only it is set; and for a private vendor read the order read, write, old.
- In CI without a write token, `--pr` fails before any file is changed or branch pushed, with the message described; with the flag it behaves as before; outside CI nothing changes.
- The guard covers all five variable names, and the test that fails without it still passes.
- No message or doc presents `VENDOR_PAT` as the name to use.
- `.vendored/pkg/git-cicd/git-cicd check --setup` passes with coverage at 99% or more for every shipped Python script and the bats tests green; `.vendored/pkg/git-semver/git-semver check-bump` passes against `origin/main`.
- The pull request into `plan/git-dev-aef7` has a passing `Verdict / git-cicd:verdict`.
- `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-aef7` reports nothing.

title: A vendor is installed through git, not the GitHub API
Resolve a vendor's versions and latest from its git tags (git ls-remote), recording the tag's commit
body:
Part of epic gv-26c4 (planning doc .pearls/docs/epics/gv-26c4.md, unit 5 of plan git-dev-aef7). Delivers into branch `plan/git-dev-aef7`. First issue of the epic: the fetch issue, the helpers issue and the validate issue build on the helpers added here.

## Why
Today `templates/install` asks the GitHub API which version is latest: `resolve_version` (templates/install:282) calls `_resolve_from_releases` (:305, `gh api repos/{repo}/releases/latest --jq .tag_name`) and falls back to `_resolve_from_version_file` (:317, `gh api repos/{repo}/contents/VERSION`, base64-decoded). `check_repo_exists` (:254, `gh api repos/{repo} --jq .full_name`) checks the vendor exists. Line numbers were re-read on the current branch (the planning doc's 256/279/291/228 were from v0.0.31, before unit 3). No commit is recorded for an installed version. The owner wants git-vendored built around git, not GitHub.

## Scope (templates/install, tests/, README.md)
1. Vendor URL: add one helper (e.g. `vendor_git_url(repo)`) that turns the configured `repo` into a URL git can fetch. The `owner/repo` shorthand (exactly one `/`, no `:`, no scheme) maps to `https://github.com/owner/repo.git`. Anything else (`https://...`, `ssh://...`, `git@host:path`, `file://...`) is passed to git unchanged.
2. Token for one git command: add one helper (e.g. `_git_env(token)`) returning a subprocess env that hands the token to git for that command only, through `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`/`GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=http.extraHeader`/`GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=Authorization: Basic <base64(x-access-token:TOKEN)>`. Also set `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` so a missing credential fails rather than hanging. The token is never put in argv or in a URL, never written to any git config file, and never printed, including in error output. Token choice is unchanged: `get_auth_token` (templates/install:233; private vendors use `read_token()` = `CICD_READ_TOKEN`, then `CICD_WRITE_TOKEN`, then `VENDOR_PAT`). Decision: a public vendor is read anonymously by git (no header when the token is empty). Reason: git reads public repos without a token on any host, and the plan wants no token for reads git can do anonymously.
3. Tag listing: one function runs `git ls-remote --tags <url>` (with `_git_env`) and returns a mapping tag -> commit. For an annotated tag the peeled `refs/tags/X^{}` line gives the commit; a lightweight tag's own sha is its commit.
4. One resolution function: `resolve_version(vendor_name, repo, requested_version, token)` stays the single place versions are resolved (the out-of-scope defective-version skip and test override will go here later). It returns the version, the tag and the commit, e.g. a small namedtuple `Resolved(version, tag, commit)`. Update every caller: `install_new_vendor` (:953), `install_existing_vendor` (:1089) and the dependency path in `resolve_deps`.
   - Version tags: `vX.Y.Z` or `X.Y.Z` with numeric dot-separated parts. Tags that are not versions (e.g. `latest`) are ignored. Tags containing `/` (a component series `<subdir>/vX.Y.Z`) are a separate series and never count for the vendor's root version. Decision: the function takes an optional tag prefix, defaulting to the root series, so a component series can be resolved later without a second resolver. Reason: the doc asks for separate series and one resolution function.
   - `latest` (or empty) means the highest version tag by numeric version order (so 0.0.10 > 0.0.9), not string order.
   - An explicit version `X` resolves to tag `vX` if it exists, else `X`. This keeps today's `v{version}`-then-`{version}` retry order from `download_and_run_install` :637/:644. If neither exists, exit with an error saying that version has no tag in that repo.
   - Decision: remove `_resolve_from_releases` and `_resolve_from_version_file` (no fallback to a `VERSION` file on the default branch). Reason: an install always reads the vendor at a tag (`v{version}`/`{version}`), so a version with no tag could never install anyway, and the doc requires that case to be reported as such. A repo with no version tags fails with an error naming the repo and saying it has no version tags.
   - `check_repo_exists` (:254) is replaced by this listing. If `git ls-remote` fails (no such repo, or no access), the error keeps today's wording: `::error::Cannot access repo: <repo>`, plus a hint that a private vendor needs `CICD_READ_TOKEN`. Drop the old line naming `GH_TOKEN`.
5. Record the commit: the commit of the installed tag is written with the version. Decision: a new file `.vendored/manifests/<vendor>.commit` (one line, 40-hex sha) is written next to `<vendor>.version` wherever `write_manifest_version` (:361) is called (`install_new_vendor` ~:1043, `install_existing_vendor` ~:1122, the dep path). Reason: `<vendor>.version` is read as a bare version by `get_current_version`, `--list`, `templates/check` and other tools, so changing its format would break readers. Also add the `.commit` file to the protected manifest set in `templates/check` (next to `.version` at templates/check:228-229) and to the files `templates/remove` deletes (templates/remove:164-168).
6. Moved tag: in `install_existing_vendor`, when the target version equals the installed one and a `<vendor>.commit` is recorded that differs from the tag's current commit, print `::warning::<vendor>: tag <tag> now points at <new sha>, recorded <old sha>`. Decision: still skip unless `--force`; a forced reinstall records the new commit. No warning when nothing is recorded (installs made before this change); the commit is recorded on their next install. Reason: refusing a moved tag is out of scope for this unit; the acceptance criterion only requires the install to say so.
7. README.md: replace the vendor-contract line `Version discovery — either GitHub Releases (tags like v1.0.0) or a VERSION file at repo root` (README.md:163) with: versions are the repo's version tags; `latest` is the highest; non-version tags and `<subdir>/v...` tags are ignored. Document `.vendored/manifests/<vendor>.commit` next to the `.version` lines (README.md:49 and :190) and the moved-tag warning.

## Out of scope
Fetching the vendor checkout and removing `gh api` from `check_install_sh`/`download_*` (sibling issue), `validate` (sibling issue), skipping defective versions, test overrides.

## Tests (tests/test_install.py; fixtures in tests/conftest.py)
- Add a conftest fixture that builds a local git repo used as a vendor (`git init`, commits made with `-c user.name=t -c user.email=t@t`, and both lightweight and annotated tags), addressed by a `file://` URL. Isolate git from the user's config (`GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null`, `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`) for the fixture's git commands. No network, and no test reads a token from the environment (the existing `_no_ambient_tokens` autouse fixture in tests/conftest.py stays in force).
- Cases: latest picks the numeric max (0.0.9 vs 0.0.10); `latest` and non-version tags are ignored; `sub/v9.9.9` is ignored for the root series and resolvable with the prefix; explicit `vX` vs bare `X`; a missing version gives the no-tag error; a repo with no version tags; a nonexistent repo gives the Cannot-access error; an annotated tag records the peeled commit, not the tag object; `owner/repo` maps to the github.com URL (a unit test, no network); `_git_env` puts the token only in GIT_CONFIG_* env (not argv, not printed) and none when the token is empty; `.commit` is written on add and upgrade; the moved-tag warning appears when the recorded commit differs, and not when nothing is recorded; check protects `.commit`; remove deletes it.
- Remove or replace tests that exercised `_resolve_from_releases`/`_resolve_from_version_file`/`check_repo_exists` through stubbed `gh api`.

## Acceptance criteria
- `grep -n 'gh", "api' templates/install` finds no call in `resolve_version` or its helpers, and `check_repo_exists`'s `gh api` is gone.
- `resolve_version` is the only function that turns a requested version into a tag and a commit; every caller uses it.
- The installed version's commit is in `.vendored/manifests/<vendor>.commit`; a reinstall of the same version whose tag moved prints the warning.
- `ci/test.sh` passes: each of the six shipped Python scripts and their total stay at 99% or more line coverage.
- `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-aef7` passes. Only `templates/`, `install.sh`, `validate`, `README.md`, `docs/` and `tests/` change, never the installed copies under `.vendored/`.
- VERSION: not raised. The integration branch is already above `main` (unit 3), and this is not breaking for git-cicd or git-semver, which are tagged releases. If implementation finds it breaks a vendor or adopter, raise it with `.vendored/pkg/git-semver/git-semver bump minor --no-commit` and say so in the PR description.

title: Fetch a vendor once with git at its version tag and read install.sh, deps.json and the schema from that checkout
body:
Part of epic gv-26c4 (planning doc .pearls/docs/epics/gv-26c4.md, unit 5 of plan git-dev-aef7). Delivers into branch `plan/git-dev-aef7`. Depends on gv-26c4.1 (`vendor_git_url`, `_git_env`, the tag listing and `resolve_version` returning version/tag/commit).

## Why
Each file of an install is a separate GitHub API call today: `check_install_sh` (templates/install:267, `gh api repos/{repo}/contents/install.sh --jq .name`), `download_deps` (:399, `gh api repos/{repo}/contents/deps.json?ref={ref}`), `download_schema` (:419, `gh api repos/{repo}/contents/templates/config.schema?ref={ref}`) and `download_and_run_install` (:621, `gh api .../contents/install.sh?ref=v{version}`, retried at :644 with `?ref={version}`). Line numbers were re-read on the current branch; the planning doc's 241/373/393/595 were from v0.0.31. A vendor on another git host cannot be installed.

## Scope (templates/install, tests/, README.md)
1. One fetch per vendor install: a function (e.g. `fetch_vendor(repo, tag, token)`) creates a temporary directory outside the repository (`tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix=gv-vendor-)` in the system temp dir) and runs `git clone --depth 1 --branch <tag> --quiet -c advice.detachedHead=false <vendor_git_url(repo)> <tmp>` with `_git_env(token)` from gv-26c4.1. The token goes to git for this one command only: never in argv or the URL, never written to config, never printed. Use it as a context manager (or try/finally) so the directory is removed afterwards, also when the install exits with an error (`sys.exit` raises SystemExit, so `finally` runs). `--depth 1` needs a URL for local repos, hence `file://` in tests. Verify the checkout's `HEAD` equals the commit `resolve_version` returned. Decision: if they differ (the tag moved between ls-remote and clone), exit with an error naming both shas. Reason: the recorded commit must be the one installed.
2. In `install_new_vendor` (:937) and `install_existing_vendor` (:1075), fetch once after `resolve_version`, then read from the checkout:
   - `check_install_sh` becomes a check that `<checkout>/install.sh` exists. Keep today's message: `::error::Repo does not implement git-vendored: <repo>` / `Expected install.sh at repository root.`. Decision: in the add path this check now runs after resolution, at the resolved tag, not on the default branch. Reason: what matters is that the version being installed has an installer.
   - `download_deps(repo, ref, token)` reads `<checkout>/deps.json`; missing or invalid JSON means None, as today.
   - `download_schema` reads `<checkout>/templates/config.schema`; missing or invalid means None, as today.
   - `download_and_run_install` runs `bash <checkout>/install.sh <version>` with cwd = the adopting repository, no temp copy of the script. The env is unchanged: `VENDOR_REPO` (the configured repo string as given: `owner/repo` stays `owner/repo`, so installers that download by themselves keep working), `VENDOR_REF` (the resolved tag, e.g. `v1.2.3`), `VENDOR_MANIFEST`, `VENDOR_INSTALL_DIR` (non-dogfood), `VENDOR_LIB`, `GH_TOKEN` as today. New: `VENDOR_CHECKOUT` = absolute path of the checkout. Decision: that name, documented in README's environment-variable table (README.md ~:170). Reason: it follows the `VENDOR_*` contract naming; the helpers issue makes `fetch_file`/`fetch_dir` consume it.
   - Dependencies resolved through `resolve_deps` each get their own fetch of their own vendor.
3. Vendor named by URL: `_is_repo_spec` (templates/install:1760) and `validate_target` (:1723) accept a git URL (`https://`, `ssh://`, `git@host:path`, `file://`) as an add target, as well as `owner/repo`. The `owner/repo` rules (exactly one `/`, non-empty parts) still apply to the shorthand, and the malformed-target rejection before any network call (README.md:60) still holds for it. The default vendor name (`install_new_vendor` :941 `repo.split('/')[-1]`, and `registered_vendor_for_repo` :1740) is the last path component with a trailing `.git` stripped. The configured `repo` field stores the target exactly as given.
4. Errors stay distinct: vendor does not exist or is not accessible (from the ls-remote in gv-26c4.1), version has no tag (gv-26c4.1), no installer at that tag (above), clone failed (an error naming the repo and tag; git's stderr is shown only after any token has been scrubbed from it).
5. Remove the now-unused `base64` decoding and `_gh_env` use on these paths if nothing else needs them. `gh pr create` (:1474) and `gh pr merge --auto` (:1499) stay; they are platform work.
6. README.md: the Adding a Vendor steps (README.md:46-50) say the vendor is fetched with git at the version's tag. The `repo` config field (README.md:147 and :223, now `GitHub repository (owner/name)`) becomes a git URL or the `owner/repo` shorthand for github.com.

## Tests (tests/test_install.py, tests/test_entrypoints.py pattern)
- Use the local `file://` vendor-repo fixture from gv-26c4.1 (no network, no token read from the environment). Its install.sh copies files from `$VENDOR_CHECKOUT` itself and writes `$VENDOR_MANIFEST`.
- End-to-end: with `gh` absent from `PATH` (a PATH of a temp bin dir holding only git, bash and coreutils), run the installer as a program (as tests/test_entrypoints.py does, keeping `COVERAGE_PROCESS_START`/`GIT_VENDORED_ROOT` via conftest's env handling). Add the vendor from `file://...`, then tag a new version in the fixture and upgrade. Both succeed, and `.files`, `.version` and `.commit` are correct.
- Cases: deps.json and the schema are read from the checkout at the tag (a change on the default branch after the tag is not seen); no install.sh at the tag gives the not-implemented error; the temp checkout is gone after success and after a failing install.sh; `VENDOR_CHECKOUT` is set and absolute; the HEAD/commit mismatch error; a URL target is accepted and named by basename without `.git`; malformed `owner/repo` is still rejected before any git call.
- Replace the tests that stub `gh api` for these functions.

## Acceptance criteria
- `grep -n 'api' templates/install` finds no `gh api` call on the add, update, deps or schema paths. Only `gh pr create` and `gh pr merge` remain as gh calls.
- With `gh` absent from `PATH`, a vendor is installed and upgraded from a `file://` vendor repo in the tests.
- The checkout directory is outside the repository and removed afterwards in every case.
- `ci/test.sh` passes with each shipped Python script and the total at 99% or more line coverage.
- `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-aef7` passes; only `templates/`, `README.md` and `tests/` change, never the installed copies under `.vendored/`.
- VERSION not raised: the integration branch is already above main (unit 3), and the change is not breaking. If it turns out breaking for a vendor or adopter, bump minor and say so in the PR description.

title: fetch_file/fetch_dir and the bootstrap install.sh copy from the vendor checkout; document a platform-neutral vendor contract
body:
Part of epic gv-26c4 (planning doc .pearls/docs/epics/gv-26c4.md, unit 5 of plan git-dev-aef7). Delivers into branch `plan/git-dev-aef7`. Depends on gv-26c4.2, which fetches the vendor checkout and passes its absolute path to install.sh as `VENDOR_CHECKOUT`.

## Why
The files an installer copies come from the GitHub API or raw.githubusercontent.com. In `templates/lib/vendor-helpers.sh`, `_vendor_download` (line 32) tries `gh api repos/$repo/contents/$repo_path?ref=$ref` (line 49) and falls back to `curl` on `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/$repo/$ref/$repo_path` (lines 57, 61). `fetch_file` (line 77) uses it, and `fetch_dir` (line 103) lists directories with `gh api .../contents/...` (line 126). git-vendored's own bootstrap, `install.sh`, has its own `fetch_file` (install.sh:34-45: gh api when GH_TOKEN is set, else curl on raw.githubusercontent.com). The planning doc's line numbers 30/75/101 were from v0.0.31 and are corrected here.

## Scope
1. `templates/lib/vendor-helpers.sh`: when `VENDOR_CHECKOUT` is set and is a directory, `_vendor_download <repo_path> <dest>` copies `$VENDOR_CHECKOUT/<repo_path>` to `<dest>`; no gh, no curl, no token. A missing source file returns nonzero with an error naming the path. Decision: copy content only (`cat src > dest` after `mkdir -p`), not the source's mode, so file modes stay what today's curl/gh download gives (umask default, +x only via `fetch_file ... +x`). Reason: the acceptance criterion asks for an install byte-identical to v0.0.31, and git checkouts carry exec bits the old download path never set.
2. `fetch_dir` in checkout mode walks `$VENDOR_CHECKOUT/<repo_path>` instead of calling `gh api`. It recurses into directories and calls `fetch_file` for each regular file, so the manifest is appended exactly as today. It skips `.git` and, to match the API mode, which only handled `type` `file` and `dir`, also skips symlinks and submodule entries. A missing directory prints `Error: failed to list directory <repo_path> from <repo>` and returns 1, as today.
3. With `VENDOR_CHECKOUT` unset or empty (an installer run by hand, or an older framework), both helpers behave exactly as today: gh api, then the curl fallback. Update the header comment's Environment list (vendor-helpers.sh:12-20) to add `VENDOR_CHECKOUT`. A vendor's own install.sh needs no change. An installer that downloads by itself keeps working, because `VENDOR_REPO`/`VENDOR_REF` are unchanged.
4. `install.sh` (repo root, git-vendored's own installer): its `fetch_file` (install.sh:34-45) copies from `$VENDOR_CHECKOUT` when set, in the same way and with the same mode rule. Otherwise it behaves as today. Update its header comment (install.sh:7-12).
5. Docs:
   - README.md bootstrap (README.md:21 `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mangimangi/git-vendored/v0.0.28/install.sh | bash -s 0.0.28`). The primary way is git: from the target repo root, `git clone --depth 1 --branch v<X.Y.Z> https://github.com/mangimangi/git-vendored.git <tmpdir>`, then `VENDOR_CHECKOUT=<tmpdir> bash <tmpdir>/install.sh <X.Y.Z>`, then remove `<tmpdir>`. Keep the curl one-liner as the GitHub-specific shortcut. Decision: the example uses the current `VERSION` value rather than the stale 0.0.28. Reason: the example should install a release that exists and is current.
   - README.md vendor contract (README.md ~:160-176): a vendor is a git repository with version tags (`vX.Y.Z`) and an `install.sh` at its root, without naming a platform. Add `VENDOR_CHECKOUT` to the env table. Reword `VENDOR_REPO`'s purpose (`owner/repo for API calls`) as the vendor's repo as configured.
   - docs/adoption.md (`$VENDOR_LIB` section lines 8-66: the fetch_file/fetch_dir docs and the env table at ~:66) and docs/vendor-install-dir-guide.md: describe checkout mode and fallback mode. In the inline-fallback example (adoption.md:18-21), show copying from `$VENDOR_CHECKOUT` when set before the curl line.

## Tests (bats, tests/bats/vendor-helpers.bats, tests/bats/install.bats, using tests/bats/stubs.bash)
- vendor-helpers.bats covers both modes. Checkout mode: `fetch_file` copies bytes exactly (including a binary/multi-line file), `+x` sets exec, no `+x` leaves the umask mode even if the source is executable, gh and curl stubs are called 0 times even with a token set, the manifest is appended, and a missing source returns nonzero. `fetch_dir` recursive copy, with `.git` and symlinks skipped, manifest lines match the API mode for the same tree, and a missing dir returns 1. Fallback mode: the existing tests stay, run with `VENDOR_CHECKOUT` unset, plus one with it set to empty.
- install.bats: the bootstrap with `VENDOR_CHECKOUT` copies every file and calls no gh/curl. Without it, behaviour is unchanged (existing tests).
- tests/test_vendor_helpers.py, if it covers the same functions, gets the same two-mode cases.
- Byte-identical check (acceptance: an existing vendor, git-cicd or git-semver, installs and upgrades unchanged and what lands on disk is byte-identical to an install by v0.0.31). Decision: an automated test builds a local `file://` vendor repo whose install.sh uses `fetch_file`/`fetch_dir` the way git-cicd's and git-semver's do (nested dirs, a `+x` file, a workflow file outside `VENDOR_INSTALL_DIR`). It installs it once through checkout mode and once through the fallback mode (gh stubbed to serve the same tree), then asserts identical files, bytes, modes and manifest. Add a manual check recorded in the PR description: in a scratch repo, install git-cicd and git-semver at their current versions with this branch's framework and with v0.0.31's, then upgrade each, and `diff -r` shows no difference. Reason: tests may not reach the network, so the real vendors can only be compared by hand.

## Acceptance criteria
- `grep -n 'gh api\|raw.githubusercontent' templates/lib/vendor-helpers.sh install.sh` matches only lines inside the fallback branch (no checkout given).
- A vendor install.sh that uses the helpers, run by the framework with `gh` absent from PATH, installs from the checkout.
- bats tests cover both helper modes; `bats tests/bats/` and `ci/test.sh` pass, with Python coverage still at 99% or more.
- README states the vendor contract without naming a platform, and documents the git bootstrap first and the curl one-liner as the GitHub shortcut.
- `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-aef7` passes; only `templates/`, `install.sh`, `README.md`, `docs/` and `tests/` change (never `.vendored/lib/vendor-helpers.sh` or other installed copies).
- VERSION not raised (the integration branch is already above main; non-breaking: installers keep working unchanged). If it turns out breaking for an adopter, bump minor and say so in the PR description.

title: validate checks a vendor with git: same tag listing and fetch as install, accepts a URL or owner/repo
body:
Part of epic gv-26c4 (planning doc .pearls/docs/epics/gv-26c4.md, unit 5 of plan git-dev-aef7). Delivers into branch `plan/git-dev-aef7`. Depends on gv-26c4.1 (tag listing, `resolve_version`, `vendor_git_url`, `_git_env`) and gv-26c4.2 (`fetch_vendor` checkout, `VENDOR_CHECKOUT`). gv-26c4.3 (helpers' checkout mode) is needed for helper-using vendors to validate offline.

## Why
`validate` (repo root) makes six `gh api` calls of the kinds the installer used, in its lines 83-171 (the planning doc said 87-161 at v0.0.31): `check_repo_exists` (:83, `gh api repos/{repo}`), `check_install_sh_exists` (:97, `gh api repos/{repo}/contents/install.sh`), `check_version_resolvable` (:111, `releases/latest` at :121 then `contents/VERSION` at :131), and `download_install_sh` (:149, `contents/install.sh?ref=v{version}` at :154, retried with `?ref={version}` at :161).

## Scope (validate, tests/test_validate.py)
1. Same code as the install: decision: `validate` loads `templates/install` as a module (`importlib.machinery.SourceFileLoader` on `os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), 'templates', 'install')`) and calls its tag listing, `resolve_version`-level resolution and `fetch_vendor`, instead of keeping its own copies. Reason: the doc requires the same fetch and tag listing as an install, and `validate` only ships in this repository next to `templates/install` (install.sh does not install it). Use variants that report instead of exiting, or catch `SystemExit` around them, so a failure becomes a failed check rather than ending validate.
2. Check mapping, with names and messages unchanged:
   - Check 1 `Repo exists`: `git ls-remote` succeeds; failure gives `cannot access <repo>`.
   - Check 3 `Version resolvable`: a version tag resolves (`latest` = highest version tag; an explicit version must have tag `v<version>` or `<version>`). Decision: the failure detail becomes `no version tags found` (or `no tag for <version>`) instead of `no releases or VERSION file found`. Reason: the old message names a source that no longer exists.
   - Then the vendor is fetched once at that tag into a temp dir outside the repo, removed afterwards.
   - Check 2 `install.sh exists`: `<checkout>/install.sh` exists; failure gives `no install.sh at root of <repo>`. Decision: report the checks in today's order 1, 2, 3, ... even though check 2 is evaluated after resolution. If resolution fails, check 2 falls back to `git ls-remote`-only info and fails with `skipped (no version)`. Reason: the output stays as close as possible to today's.
   - Checks 4-5 (shebang, `bash -n`) read `<checkout>/install.sh`.
   - Checks 6-8 (dry-run, manifest written, manifest files exist) run as today in the sandbox, with `VENDOR_CHECKOUT` set to the checkout. Decision: also set `VENDOR_LIB` to this repo's `templates/lib/vendor-helpers.sh`. Reason: a helper-using vendor then validates from the checkout with no network; validate sets no VENDOR_LIB today, so helper-using vendors fall back to curl.
3. Accept a URL or `owner/repo`: `validate <target>` takes a git URL (`https://`, `ssh://`, `git@host:path`, `file://`) or `owner/repo` (= github.com), via `vendor_git_url`. Sandbox vendor name (`run_dryrun_install` `repo.split('/')[-1]`) strips a trailing `.git`. Update the usage docstring (validate:1-12) and argparse help. `ci/validate.sh` and the README validate-job text (README.md:367, `repo (owner/repo, required)`) say a URL is also accepted.
4. Token: unchanged source (`get_auth_token`: GH_TOKEN, then GITHUB_TOKEN). It is handed to git with `_git_env` for each command only, never printed, never written to config. With no token, git reads anonymously.
5. Remove validate's own `gh api` calls, its `base64` decoding and `_gh_env` where unused.

## Tests (tests/test_validate.py, tests/bats/ci-validate.bats if its messages change)
- Use the `file://` vendor-repo fixture from gv-26c4.1 (no network, no token read from the environment). Run validate with `gh` absent from `PATH` against a good vendor: every check passes and it exits 0. Run it as a program at least once (tests/test_entrypoints.py pattern) so coverage counts.
- Failure cases: nonexistent repo; no version tags; explicit version with no tag; no install.sh at the tag; bad shebang; syntax error; install.sh that writes no manifest; manifest listing a missing file. Each gives its check's existing name and message, apart from the version-resolvable detail above.
- Parity: for the same fixture, validate and the installer resolve the same version and commit.
- Replace the tests that stub `gh api`.

## Acceptance criteria
- `grep -n 'gh' validate` finds no `gh api` call and no `raw.githubusercontent.com`.
- With `gh` absent from PATH, `validate file://<fixture>` passes in the tests on the vendor that the install tests install and upgrade.
- Check names and messages are unchanged except the version-resolvable failure detail.
- `ci/test.sh` passes with `validate` and every other shipped Python script at 99% or more line coverage.
- `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-aef7` passes; only `validate`, `ci/validate.sh`, `README.md` and `tests/` change.
- VERSION not raised (the integration branch is already above main; non-breaking). If it turns out breaking, bump minor and say so in the PR description.
